# Session guard: legacy path

The `storybloq_session_guard` tool answers "is anything running, and may I write?"
in one call. This file is what to do when you cannot use its answer directly.
Everything below is the same classification the tool applies, generated from the
same source, so the two cannot drift apart.

## Entry modes

There are two ways to arrive here and **they do not share an input.** Read the one
that applies.

### Mode A: tool absent

**Reached when:** Both broad and targeted tool discovery fail to surface storybloq_session_guard, OR an explicit unknown-tool error -- AND storybloq_status is reachable. If no storybloq_* tool is reachable at all, this mode does not apply: its first instruction is a status call, so go to the Step 0 setup/CLI-fallback path instead.

**Input:** Call storybloq_status with {"format":"json"}, apply the deduplication rule below, then classify each surviving summary with the tables below. If that status call FAILS TO EXECUTE, rather than returning a payload, this mode has no input and stops: report the error and apply the **Step 0.5 execution-failure rule**, whose sole authoritative definition lives in Step 0 and is not restated or renamed here. Apply the **Step 0.5 execution-failure rule** in Step 0; that rule is authoritative and is not restated here. That is distinct from the older-server case below, where the call succeeds but the JSON format is unavailable, and distinct again from a payload that is missing an array (see Policies). When the call SUCCEEDS, retain the payload: the source says to reuse this status result during context loading, so it becomes Step 2's Project status result and no second `storybloq_status` call is made. A second call is a fresh observation of the filesystem taken AFTER the ownership decision, so the context you present could describe a different state than the one you classified. If the JSON format was unavailable and you classified from the single permitted MARKDOWN response instead, that response is still the payload you retain: reuse it as Step 2's Project status result and SKIP Step 2's reconciliation, because this path made ONE observation and reconciliation exists only to close the gap between two. Make no further status call either way.

### Mode B: multi-session

**Reached when:** The guard returned overallAction: null (more than one bearing session).

**Input:** Consume the sessions array already returned by the guard, without rescanning and without reclassifying. Report every session and its verdict, and report that the conflict between them is unresolved: the source prescribes an action per session and says nothing about combining them, so a permissive verdict standing beside a restrictive one settles nothing. Do not treat it as having settled it -- that is the ISS-554 shape, working beside a live foreign session. Letting the permissive verdict win, letting the restrictive one win, and refusing to act at all are three resolutions the source supports equally, which is to say not at all; choosing among them is ISS-898's decision. **Do not call `storybloq_status` again.**

Rescanning is not a harmless double-check. A second read is a fresh observation of
the filesystem: a session can start, end, or expire in between, so you would apply
these rules to a set that never produced the verdict you are responding to. Worse,
if the rescan happens to return a single bearing session you would silently resolve
a multiplicity the guard deliberately declined to resolve, which is
first-session-wins reintroduced through a race.

**Do not reclassify.** Each entry in that array is already a decided verdict: it
carries its own `relationship`, `action`, and capability flags. Re-deriving them
from the tables below is how the tool and the legacy path drift apart, and nothing
would catch it -- you would not have rescanned, so a no-rescan check still passes.
Each verdict's `action` names what the source procedure prescribes FOR THAT
SESSION, and "Acting on a verdict" below sets out each one in full. The tables in
this file are Mode A's classifier; in Mode B they are reference material only.

**There is no aggregate rule, and this file will not invent one.** Mode B is
reached because the guard already found more than one bearing session, so the
`multiple` row of "Aggregating across sessions" below is your case. Read it
there: it is shared with Mode A rather than stated here, because a rule kept in
one mode's block is a rule the other mode never reads.

## Aggregating across sessions

**Both modes reach this section, and Mode A reaches it by the ordinary path.**
Mode A's input is a whole status payload, so it classifies EVERY session that
survives, and can easily hold two verdicts. This section is placed here because
it defines what the final answer looks like, but it is applied LAST: Mode A must
first apply "Deduplicate before classifying", then the ordered gates, then the
ownership tables, all rendered below, and return here only with the surviving
verdicts in hand. Combining them is not left to judgement; there is exactly one
rule per population size, and it is the same rule the tool applies.

- **no session survives deduplication and every rule in Gate order** (`none`) -> `overallAction`: `free`

  Nothing bears on this project, so the guard imposes nothing: proceed with the requested work. With no session verdict to constrain the invocation, there is nothing to weigh: proceed with the requested work.

  > Provenance: Step 0.5 constrains an invocation only when a session exists; with none, no row applies and no restriction is in force.

- **exactly one session survives deduplication and every rule in Gate order** (`single`) -> `overallAction`: `<that session's own action>`

  The aggregate IS that session's verdict, unchanged. Apply its procedure from `Acting on a verdict` in full.

  > Provenance: Step 0.5 prescribes an action per session; with one session there is nothing to combine, so the per-session rule stands as the answer.

- **two or more sessions survive deduplication and every rule in Gate order** (`multiple`) -> `overallAction`: **none** (the tool returns `null`)

  There is NO aggregate. Report every session with its own verdict, state plainly that the conflict between them is unresolved, and select none of them. Do not act on the first, the most permissive, or the one matching your own task. A `continue` or `auto-resume` sitting beside a `monitor-only` is an unresolved hazard, not a permission. Deciding the rule is ISS-898.

  > Provenance: The prose evaluates sessions one at a time and supplies no ordering, suppression, or winner. The three available resolutions (permissive wins, restrictive wins, refuse to act) are equally unsupported, so the classifier reports no aggregate and this file invents none.

## Acting on a verdict

Mode A arrives here after classifying with the tables below. In Mode B these are
what each verdict MEANS, not an instruction to execute one while another session's
verdict contradicts it.

These are the procedures in full, not summaries of them. In Mode A an abbreviated
instruction is a behavior change: where the section above yields a single action to
apply, Mode A acts on it, so a dropped argument or a missing branch changes what
gets called. Reaching a procedure at all requires that the aggregate above named
one; under `multiple` no procedure is selected. In Mode B
they are REFERENCE definitions -- what each verdict means, for reporting -- and must
not be used to select or execute an action while the aggregate conflict is
unresolved.

`resumable` reports whether the server will accept a `resume` call. It is
informational: do not use it to DECIDE whether to make one. It appears in one
procedure below, `monitor-only`, and only as corroboration when explaining that
a takeover call cannot be formed without a caller identity. What stops that call
is the missing `clientTaskId`, a fact about the input rather than a policy read
off this flag.

Be plain about what that costs: stopping there is observably a CLIENT-SIDE
REFUSAL, so the call U2 historically issued is no longer issued and no server
rejection is observed. T-446 took that deliberately, as a recorded exception to
its own transcribe-do-not-fix rule, because the alternative is prescribing a call
that cannot be formed. ISS-898 case 2 now owns only the REPRESENTATION question:
whether this row should advertise the capability at all, or report it unavailable
up front.

### `continue`

Your own task. Do not show an Active Autonomous Session banner and do not ask for Resume. Process owner replies such as `Ratify T-020` directly. One concise line such as `Continuing T-020 in IMPLEMENT` is enough.

### `auto-resume`

Call `storybloq_autonomous_guide` with the full `sessionId`, `action: "resume"`, and `clientTaskId` when a task id resolved, then continue the pipeline. Do not ask for another confirmation. If identity is UNAVAILABLE, omit `clientTaskId` rather than inventing or nulling one: this reaches an ownerless legacy COMPACT session, where the guide preserves legacy resume behavior without binding a new `ownerTask`, and the verdict's `bindsOwner: false` says so. `bindsOwner` is about `ownerTask` alone; it makes no claim about `claudeCodeSessionId`.

### `monitor-only`

BRANCH ON `relationship` FIRST; this one action name covers two different UX cells and they are not interchangeable. If `relationship` is `foreign-live`, render ordinary foreign-task UX: the owner task exists and can be named, opened, and relayed to. If `relationship` is `unowned-legacy`, there IS no owner task, so offer ONLY Monitor or work here on something else -- do not name an owner, do not offer Open task, do not relay, and do not describe the session as belonging to another task, because ownership is precisely what cannot be verified. In BOTH cases: do not mention recovery and do not ask about takeover. Recovery becomes reachable ONLY when the user explicitly asks for it AND `recoveryRequiresExplicitRequest && resumePermittedByProse && requiresTakeover` are all true. If one of those three is false, explain why recovery is unavailable and stop. When all three ARE true, CHECK CALLER IDENTITY BEFORE ANYTHING ELSE, and before asking the user to confirm anything: the prescribed call requires a CURRENT `clientTaskId`, and when identity is unavailable there is none. If there is no current `clientTaskId`: do NOT ask the user to confirm the recorded owner is gone, do not invent an id, do not pass null, and do not omit it -- omitting it makes the call mean something the source never describes, since takeover semantics are defined in terms of binding the current task. Report that the prose permits the request while the call it prescribes cannot be formed, and stop. Asking for a destructive-looking confirmation first and only then revealing that nothing can happen is the worse version of this. `resumable: false` corroborates that the guide would reject the call; it is not the reason for stopping. Only with a resolved current `clientTaskId`: confirm the recorded owner task is gone, then call `resume` once with the full `sessionId`, that `clientTaskId`, and `takeover: true`.

### `offer-recovery`

Offer Resume here, End session, or Back. Resume only after explicit selection, passing the full `sessionId` and `clientTaskId` when a task id resolved; successful recovery rebinds ownership, meaning it binds `ownerTask` to the recovering task. End session enters the typed cancellation flow. If identity is UNAVAILABLE, omit `clientTaskId` rather than inventing or nulling one: the guide accepts the call, and no new `ownerTask` is bound and any `ownerTask` already recorded is preserved. Ownership is not untouched at the field level: Recovery derives `claudeCodeSessionId` from an existing `ownerTask`: it writes a CLAUDE owner's id, CLEARS the field for a codex owner (the field is claude's), and preserves it only when no `ownerTask` exists. (ISS-898 case 3)

### `unverifiable`

The session's state, lease, identity, or reported session population could not be determined. Stop and tell the user to run `storybloq session list`. Do not guess and do not offer Resume.

### `free`

Nothing is running. Continue to argument routing.

### `sessionstart-on-request` (fallback only)

Do not offer recovery and do not present a menu. Only after the user asks to continue, follow the SessionStart resume instruction; the guide remains authoritative. Reached only from the `json-status-compact` policy, never from a guard verdict: the guard emits no such action, because a server that can answer the guard can answer JSON status too.

## Deduplicate before classifying

> Read both `activeSessions` and `resumableSessions`; deduplicate by full `sessionId`.

Before classifying anything, collapse records that share a full `sessionId` to one. Read `activeSessions` first, then `resumableSessions`, and keep the first occurrence of each id. Order within each array by `sourceDir` when the payload carries it, and otherwise keep the order the server returned: mode A exists for servers old enough to lack the typed guard, and their status summaries may predate `sourceDir` entirely, so a rule that required it would leave those payloads with no executable order at all. Without this, one session recorded under two directories counts twice, and two bearing sessions have no aggregate rule at all -- so a duplicate would route you into the multi-session fallback for what this document counts as one session. The prose names no tiebreak; first-by-read-order is this file's deterministic choice, not a rule it found, and the dropped directory is reported rather than discarded silently (ISS-897). Reporting is CONDITIONAL on having directories to name: an older mode A payload may carry no `sourceDir`, and then there is no selector to report. In that case say that two records shared one `sessionId` and that their source directories are unavailable; do not fabricate a selector, and do not silently drop the collision unreported.

A record can violate more than one rule below. It stops at the FIRST gate in this
list, which is the order the tool evaluates them in. Read this list, not the
section order: these gates are deliberately not grouped by topic, and
`recovery-not-compact` runs AFTER the terminal and unknown-state gates even
though it sits in the population section with its siblings.

1. `active-lease-not-live` -- see "Population invariants"
2. `recovery-lease-live` -- see "Population invariants"
3. `recovery-not-pending` -- see "Population invariants"
4. `terminal-session-end` -- see "Terminal sessions"
5. `unknown-workflow-state` -- see "Undetermined session state"
6. `recovery-not-compact` -- see "Population invariants"

Every gate here yields `indeterminate` / `unverifiable` with all capabilities
false. They differ only in which one you cite, so citing the wrong one is a
reporting error rather than an authorization error -- but report the first.

## Terminal sessions

Gate `terminal-session-end`.

`SESSION_END` is a VALID workflow state and never a BEARING one. The scanner drops it outright, so neither `activeSessions` nor `resumableSessions` can legitimately contain it, and a record carrying it did not come from a scan. Classify it `indeterminate` / `unverifiable` with every capability false, BEFORE consulting the ownership tables, and tell the user to run `storybloq session list`. Do not read its membership in the valid set below as permission to treat it as an ordinary non-COMPACT state: that path ends at `continue` for its owner, which is an actionable verdict for a session that has ENDED. The typed guard returns `unverifiable` here, and this rule exists so mode A reaches the same answer rather than the opposite one.

| Population | `state` | `compactPending` | `leaseState` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `activeSessions`, `resumableSessions` | `SESSION_END` | `any` | `any` |

> Basis: Same basis as the population invariants and registered the same way: the prose has no sentence about a terminal session appearing in either population, so this rule is transcribed from the `terminal-session-end` gate in `PRE_OWNERSHIP_GATES`. It is a transcription of OBSERVED behavior, not a citation, and its declared domain is parity-tested against that predicate across BOTH populations rather than asserted.

| State | Relationship | Action | Resume permitted | Server accepts | Takeover | Explicit request | Binds new ownerTask |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `SESSION_END` | `indeterminate` | `unverifiable` | no | no | no | no | no |

Each array carries its own promise about the records inside it. A record that

no ownership row applies to it. Every one of these is

to tell the user to run `storybloq session list`.

Each row states the rule's FULL domain. `any` means the rule does not read that
field at all, so it fires for every value: these are conditions, not examples.

| Population | `state` | `compactPending` | `leaseState` | Rule |

| `activeSessions` | `any` | `any` | `expired`, `missing`, `invalid` | `active-lease-not-live` |
| `resumableSessions` | `any` | `any` | `live` | `recovery-lease-live` |

| `resumableSessions` | any except `COMPACT` | `any` | `any` | `recovery-not-compact` |

## Undetermined session state

Gate `unknown-workflow-state`.

Checked BEFORE ownership, and independent of it, which is why it is placed
ahead of the verdict tables rather than after them: a reader working through
this file in order must decide this question before reaching a row that assumes
the state is valid. The scanner substitutes
`"unknown"` for an absent `state` and copies through whatever string is present,
while every ownership row branches on `state === "COMPACT"` -- so without this
check an undetermined state reads as a valid non-COMPACT one, and a same-owner
caller could be told to `continue` a session that actually needs COMPACT
recovery.

**The rule.** Before classifying ownership, check the session's `state` against the valid set. If it is not in that set -- including the scanner's `"unknown"` substitute for an absent field, and any typo or unrecognized value -- the verdict is `indeterminate` / `unverifiable` with every capability false. Do not fall through to the ownership tables: every row there branches on `state === "COMPACT"`, so an unrecognized state would be read as a valid non-COMPACT one and could return `continue` for a session that actually needs COMPACT recovery.

**The valid set**, which is the same list the classifier checks against:

`INIT`, `LOAD_CONTEXT`, `PICK_TICKET`, `PLAN`, `PLAN_REVIEW`, `IMPLEMENT`, `WRITE_TESTS`, `TEST`, `CODE_REVIEW`, `BUILD`, `VERIFY`, `FINALIZE`, `COMPACT`, `HANDOVER`, `COMPLETE`, `LESSON_CAPTURE`, `ISSUE_FIX`, `ISSUE_SWEEP`, `SESSION_END`

Anything else, without exception. Examples:

- **S1** live session, `state` absent (scanner substitutes "unknown"), any owner, any caller identity -> `indeterminate` / `unverifiable`, every capability false.
  > If state, lease, or full identity still cannot be determined, stop and tell the user to run `storybloq session list`; do not guess.
- **S2** live session, `state` present but not a workflow state (for example "IMPLEMNT") -> `indeterminate` / `unverifiable`, every capability false.
  > If state, lease, or full identity still cannot be determined, stop and tell the user to run `storybloq session list`; do not guess.

## Configurations that produce no verdict

- **8-expired** COMPACT, compactPending FALSE, lease expired. activeSessions requires leaseState === live; resumableSessions requires compactPending === true
- **8-missing** COMPACT, compactPending FALSE, lease missing. Same omission. The scanner's membership rule is compactPending, not lease state, so every non-live lease behaves alike here.
- **8-invalid** COMPACT, compactPending FALSE, lease invalid. Same omission.
- **9-expired** non-COMPACT, lease expired. activeSessions requires leaseState === live; resumableSessions requires state === COMPACT
- **9-missing** non-COMPACT, lease missing. Same omission.
- **9-invalid** non-COMPACT, lease invalid. Same omission.

## Policies

- **missing-arrays** (`unverifiable`): A status payload lacking `activeSessions` or `resumableSessions` is NOT an empty array. An absent key means the server did not report that population -- it is an older-server or degraded-payload signal, and the answer is unknown, not "nothing is running". Stop and tell the user to run `storybloq session list`; never proceed as though the project were free.
- **json-status-unavailable** (`monitor-only`): If JSON format is unavailable from an older server, call Markdown status once and treat a live non-COMPACT session as unverifiable legacy: Monitor or other work only.
- **json-status-compact** (`sessionstart-on-request`): For a COMPACT session on an older server that cannot return JSON status, follow a SessionStart resume instruction only after the user asks to continue; the guide remains authoritative. This is the other half of the markdown-status sentence: the non-COMPACT half is `json-status-unavailable`, and without this half the older-server COMPACT path has no rule at all. It is deliberately NOT `offer-recovery`: the prose presents no menu and makes no unsolicited offer, it waits to be asked.
- **do-not-guess** (`unverifiable`): If state, lease, or full identity still cannot be determined, stop and tell the user to run `storybloq session list`; do not guess.

## Where each row comes from

Every row and every procedure quotes the guard contract as it stood before the
typed guard existed, frozen at `test/fixtures/skill-step-0.5-pre-t446.md`. Three
regions of that document are quotable: Step 0.5 itself, the client task identity
paragraph it depends on, and the do-not-guess sentence in Step 3. A citation is
one or more COMPLETE consecutive sentences from one of them, asserted by test, so
a quote cannot be trimmed to drop the rule in its tail. Where a row rests on more
than one run of sentences, each run is rendered as its OWN blockquote and is
validated separately against a single region: the runs may come from different
regions, so presenting them as one quotation would claim a contiguity the
document does not have. That requirement covers the ownership rows, the state
gate, the deduplication rule, and the procedures below. It does NOT cover the population invariants or the
terminal-session rule: the source has no sentence about a record whose own fields
contradict the array carrying it, nor about a terminal session turning up in one,
because it never contemplates either. Those rules cite nothing and instead
declare `basis: observed-classifier` against a named production gate, with their
full domain parity-tested against it in every population they claim. A rule with neither a citation
nor that constrained basis does not belong in this file. Interpretation appears as a Note beneath the
quote, never inside it: the action names below are this tool's own vocabulary and
appear nowhere in the source document.

### Caller identity available

- **1** (same ownerTask, non-COMPACT, live)
  > Same owner, non-COMPACT: this is the current autonomous task, not a foreign session. Do not show an Active Autonomous Session banner and do not ask for Resume.
- **2** (same ownerTask, COMPACT, live)
  > Same owner, COMPACT: call `storybloq_autonomous_guide` automatically with the full `sessionId`, `action: "resume"`, and `clientTaskId`, then continue the pipeline. Do not ask for another confirmation.
- **3** (different ownerTask, non-COMPACT, live (ISS-848))
  > Different live owner, non-COMPACT: never call or offer `resume`. Follow the foreign-task UX in Step 3.
- **4** (different ownerTask, COMPACT, live)
  > Different live owner, COMPACT: do not resume automatically. Prefer Open task or Monitor. If the user explicitly asks to recover here, confirm that the recorded owner task is gone, then call `resume` once with the full `sessionId`, current `clientTaskId`, and `takeover: true`.
- **5** (no ownerTask, non-COMPACT, live)
  > Live legacy session without `ownerTask`, non-COMPACT: ownership cannot be verified. Offer only Monitor or work here on something else.
- **6** (no ownerTask, COMPACT, live (migration path))
  > Live legacy session without `ownerTask`, COMPACT: call `resume` with the full `sessionId` and current `clientTaskId`; this migration recovery binds the current task.
- **7** (COMPACT + compactPending, lease EXPIRED)
  > Expired COMPACT session: offer Resume here, End session, or Back. Resume only after explicit selection, passing the full `sessionId` and current `clientTaskId`; successful recovery rebinds ownership.
- **7b-missing** (COMPACT + compactPending, lease MISSING (undetermined, not expired))
  > If state, lease, or full identity still cannot be determined, stop and tell the user to run `storybloq session list`; do not guess.
- **7b-invalid** (COMPACT + compactPending, lease INVALID (undetermined, not expired))
  > If state, lease, or full identity still cannot be determined, stop and tell the user to run `storybloq session list`; do not guess.

### Caller identity unavailable

- **U1** (any ownerTask, non-COMPACT, live, caller has no identity)
  > Missing or malformed identity never blocks the legacy workflow, but it cannot prove same-task ownership.

  > Different live owner, non-COMPACT: never call or offer `resume`. Follow the foreign-task UX in Step 3.
- **U2** (any ownerTask, COMPACT, live, caller has no identity -- the ONLY row where resumable and resumePermittedByProse differ (ISS-898))
  > Different live owner, COMPACT: do not resume automatically. Prefer Open task or Monitor.

  > If the user explicitly asks to recover here, confirm that the recorded owner task is gone, then call `resume` once with the full `sessionId`, current `clientTaskId`, and `takeover: true`.

  > Missing or malformed identity never blocks the legacy workflow, but it cannot prove same-task ownership.

  Note: The prose does not condition the takeover offer on the CALLER having an identity, but `takeover: true` binds the recovering caller, so the guide rejects the call without one. This is the only row where `resumable` and `resumePermittedByProse` differ. T-446 records both facts in the verdict -- the capability the prose grants and the acceptance the server withholds -- and does NOT resolve the representation: the offer is still advertised. It does, however, stop the call: the prescribed `clientTaskId` cannot be formed here, so the procedure reports that and stops before any confirmation, which is observably a client-side refusal and is the execution half of ISS-898 case 2, taken deliberately. What ISS-898 case 2 still owns is whether this row should advertise the capability at all.
- **U3** (no ownerTask, non-COMPACT, live, caller has no identity)
  > Live legacy session without `ownerTask`, non-COMPACT: ownership cannot be verified. Offer only Monitor or work here on something else.
- **U4** (no ownerTask, COMPACT, live, caller has no identity)
  > Live legacy session without `ownerTask`, COMPACT: call `resume` with the full `sessionId` and current `clientTaskId`; this migration recovery binds the current task. If task identity is unavailable, the guide preserves legacy resume behavior without binding.
- **U5** (ownerTask present OR absent, COMPACT, compactPending, expired lease, caller has no identity -- offer preserved, no new `ownerTask` bound, any `ownerTask` already recorded preserved)
  > Expired COMPACT session: offer Resume here, End session, or Back. Resume only after explicit selection, passing the full `sessionId` and current `clientTaskId`; successful recovery rebinds ownership. End session enters the typed cancellation flow.

  > Missing or malformed identity never blocks the legacy workflow, but it cannot prove same-task ownership. Task identity is accidental-concurrency protection, not a security boundary; when identity is unavailable, guide ownership checks preserve the legacy fail-open behavior.

  Note: The expired-COMPACT bullet describes recovery as passing the current `clientTaskId` and rebinding ownership, neither of which is possible here, and supplies no variant for it. What IS supported is that missing identity does not block the legacy workflow, so the offer stands; `bindsOwner` is false because there is no id to bind, not because a sentence grants an exception. The prose gap is filed as ISS-898 case 3. `resumable: true` is OBSERVED, not inferred: `test/autonomous/identity-free-expired-resume.test.ts` invokes the guide with no `clientTaskId` across the whole owner axis and asserts acceptance plus the exact post-resume ownership. `bindsOwner: false` is a statement about `ownerTask` ALONE: no new owner is bound and a recorded one survives, while the legacy `claudeCodeSessionId`, which this verdict cannot see (ISS-899), is DERIVED from `ownerTask` -- written for a claude owner, CLEARED for a codex owner, and preserved only when no owner exists.
- **U6-missing** (COMPACT + compactPending, lease MISSING, caller has no identity)
  > If state, lease, or full identity still cannot be determined, stop and tell the user to run `storybloq session list`; do not guess.
- **U6-invalid** (COMPACT + compactPending, lease INVALID, caller has no identity)
  > If state, lease, or full identity still cannot be determined, stop and tell the user to run `storybloq session list`; do not guess.

### Actions

The per-action procedures above transcribe these sentences. They are cited for the
same reason the rows are: in mode A this section is the executable contract; in
mode B it documents each verdict for reporting only and authorizes no selection or
execution while the aggregate conflict is unresolved.

- **`continue`**
  > Same owner, non-COMPACT: this is the current autonomous task, not a foreign session. Do not show an Active Autonomous Session banner and do not ask for Resume. Process owner replies such as `Ratify T-020` directly. On a normal context load, one concise line such as `Continuing T-020 in IMPLEMENT` is enough.

  Note: `continue` is T-446's name for this cell. The prose has no action vocabulary; it describes the situation and the response.
- **`auto-resume`**
  > Same owner, COMPACT: call `storybloq_autonomous_guide` automatically with the full `sessionId`, `action: "resume"`, and `clientTaskId`, then continue the pipeline. Do not ask for another confirmation.

  > Live legacy session without `ownerTask`, COMPACT: call `resume` with the full `sessionId` and current `clientTaskId`; this migration recovery binds the current task. If task identity is unavailable, the guide preserves legacy resume behavior without binding.

  Note: One action name for two prose cells that prescribe the same call: same-owner COMPACT and ownerless legacy COMPACT. They differ in whether the resume binds an `ownerTask`, which `bindsOwner` carries, and therefore in whether `clientTaskId` can be passed at all.
- **`monitor-only`**
  > Different live owner, non-COMPACT: never call or offer `resume`. Follow the foreign-task UX in Step 3.

  > Different live owner, COMPACT: do not resume automatically. Prefer Open task or Monitor. If the user explicitly asks to recover here, confirm that the recorded owner task is gone, then call `resume` once with the full `sessionId`, current `clientTaskId`, and `takeover: true`.

  > Live legacy session without `ownerTask`, non-COMPACT: ownership cannot be verified. Offer only Monitor or work here on something else.

  Note: One action name for three prose cells, and the flags alone do NOT separate them. The flags settle whether RECOVERY is reachable (only the foreign-COMPACT cell sets `requiresTakeover` and `recoveryRequiresExplicitRequest`), but the UX cell is settled by `relationship`: the source gives foreign owners the Step 3 foreign-task UX and gives an ownerless legacy session `Offer only Monitor or work here on something else`, which has no owner to open or relay to. An earlier draft opened with an unconditional `Render ordinary foreign-task UX`, handing an ownerless session a flow built entirely around an owner task that does not exist. A second defect lived in the recovery branch: U2 sets all three prose flags true while `resumable` is false, so the branch was reachable and sent a reader to form a call out of a `clientTaskId` that does not exist. BE PLAIN ABOUT WHAT THIS COSTS. Stopping there is observably a CLIENT-SIDE REFUSAL, whatever the rationale, so T-446 has taken the execution-level half of ISS-898 case 2: the historically prescribed call is no longer issued for U2 and no server rejection is observed. That is a deliberate, recorded exception to this ticket's transcribe-do-not-fix rule, taken because the alternative is prescribing a call that cannot be formed. What ISS-898 case 2 still owns is the REPRESENTATION question: whether the offer should be withheld up front, and whether the verdict should mark the path unavailable rather than advertising a capability the caller cannot use.
- **`offer-recovery`**
  > Expired COMPACT session: offer Resume here, End session, or Back. Resume only after explicit selection, passing the full `sessionId` and current `clientTaskId`; successful recovery rebinds ownership. End session enters the typed cancellation flow.

  Note: The expired-COMPACT bullet describes recovery only as passing the current `clientTaskId` and rebinding, and supplies no variant for a caller with no identity. The offer is preserved there because missing identity "never blocks the legacy workflow"; that the call then binds no new `ownerTask` is a consequence, not a documented rule. "No new `ownerTask` is bound" is deliberately not "the session is unowned afterward": this row's owner axis is `any`, and a session that already had an `ownerTask` keeps it. It is also not "nothing is written": recovery derives `claudeCodeSessionId` from an existing `ownerTask`: it writes a CLAUDE owner's id, CLEARS the field for a codex owner, and preserves it only when no `ownerTask` exists. `bindsOwner` is about `ownerTask` alone. Verified against the guide across that whole axis rather than inferred: see `test/autonomous/identity-free-expired-resume.test.ts`.
- **`unverifiable`**
  > If state, lease, or full identity still cannot be determined, stop and tell the user to run `storybloq session list`; do not guess.

  > Both arrays are always present and are empty when there are no sessions, so an EMPTY array means "no sessions" and a MISSING key means the server predates that contract; treat the missing case as unverifiable and fall back as below rather than reading it as "none".

  Note: Two sentences, because the procedure names two dimensions: the do-not-guess rule covers state, lease, and identity; the empty-versus-missing array contract covers the reported session population.
- **`free`**
  > Both arrays are always present and are empty when there are no sessions, so an EMPTY array means "no sessions" and a MISSING key means the server predates that contract; treat the missing case as unverifiable and fall back as below rather than reading it as "none".

  > This guard runs on EVERY Storybloq invocation regardless of subcommand. It MUST complete before argument routing.

  Note: The prose has no bullet for "nothing is running" because it never arises as an ownership case: with both arrays empty there is no session to compare, and the guard's own instruction is to complete and let argument routing proceed.
- **`sessionstart-on-request`**
  > If JSON format is unavailable from an older server, call Markdown status once and treat a live non-COMPACT session as unverifiable legacy (Monitor or other work only). For a COMPACT session, follow a SessionStart resume instruction only after the user asks to continue; the guide remains authoritative.

  Note: Fallback-only. The guard emits no such action, because a server that can answer `storybloq_session_guard` can answer JSON status too. It exists so Mode A retains the older-server COMPACT rule, which is otherwise lost with the prose it lived in.

## Known gaps, filed not fixed

- **ISS-897** -- the scanner conceals damaged sessions. An unreadable or malformed
  `state.json`, a symlinked entry, or a record with an unexpected `status`
  silently vanishes from the scan, so the verdict reads `free` while a live
  session sits beside you.
- **ISS-898** -- (a) no aggregate rule exists for more than one bearing session,
  which is why mode B exists at all; (b) a foreign COMPACT session permits a
  takeover that the guide would reject when the caller has no identity. The OFFER
  is preserved here, because that is today's behavior; the CALL is not, because
  its required `clientTaskId` cannot be formed, so the procedure stops before
  any confirmation and no server rejection is observed. That execution half is
  T-446's deliberate exception; what remains open is whether this row should
  advertise the capability at all; (c) expired-COMPACT
  recovery is documented only as passing the current `clientTaskId` and
  rebinding ownership, with no variant for a caller that has neither. The offer
  is preserved (missing identity never blocks the legacy workflow) and the call
  is accepted by the guide. Nothing rebinds `ownerTask`: no new one is bound and
  any already recorded is preserved. The legacy field is NOT untouched: recovery
  derives `claudeCodeSessionId` from `ownerTask` wherever one is recorded,
  writing a claude owner's id and CLEARING it for a codex owner, and leaves it
  alone only when there is no owner. Both that acceptance and those
  per-field outcomes are observed rather than inferred, across the whole owner
  axis the row spans: see
  `test/autonomous/identity-free-expired-resume.test.ts`.
- **ISS-899** -- this classification ignores `claudeCodeSessionId` because Step
  0.5 never mentions it, while `liveOwnershipConflict` still resolves ownership
  through it. The two disagree in two cells, deliberately and with tests.
- **ISS-900** -- Step 0.5 says what to do when the guard tool is ABSENT (this
  file) but not when it is present and its call FAILS. Today a failure preserves the
  fail-open OUTCOME it always had, through a different ROUTE: the Step 0.5
  execution-failure rule enters the CLI context procedure directly, because the
  generic setup block has no branch for a registered-but-erroring tool.
